'''''Aeonium haworthii''''', also known as '''Haworth's aeonium''' or '''pinwheel''', is a [[species]] of [[succulent]] [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Crassulaceae]]. It is grown as a [[houseplant]] in [[temperate region]]s. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]],<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Aeonium haworthii''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/504/Aeonium-haworthii/Details | accessdate=23 February 2020}}</ref> as has the cultivar 'Variegatum'.<ref name=":0">{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/83865/i-Aeonium-haworthii-i-Variegatum-(v)/Details
| title = ''Aeonium haworthii'' 'Variegatum'
| publisher = Royal Horticultural Society
| accessdate = 3 January 2018}}</ref>

==Distribution==
''A. haworthii'' is [[native plant|native]] to the [[Canary Islands]] and northern [[Africa]], but it has been introduced to other areas of similar climate, such as [[Southern California]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Aeonium haworthii 'Kiwi'|url=https://www.gardenersworld.com/plants/aeonium-haworthii-kiwi/|access-date=2021-04-07|website=BBC Gardeners' World Magazine|language=en}}</ref> In the [[United States|US]], it is suitable to be grown outside in [[Hardiness zone|USDA hardiness zones]] 9–11.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=2019-06-01|title=Aeonium Haworthii Care: Growing Pinwheel Plants|url=https://plantcaretoday.com/aeonium-haworthii.html|access-date=2021-04-07|website=Plant Care Today|language=en-US}}</ref> This species is [[Drought-tolerant plant|drought tolerant]] and prefers full sun.<ref name="kernock.co.uk">{{Cite web|title=Kernock Park Plants Ltd Aeonium haworthii 'Bicolor'|url=https://www.kernock.co.uk/acatalog/info_U6344.html|access-date=2021-04-07|website=www.kernock.co.uk}}</ref> It is sometimes susceptible to [[aphid]]s and [[mealybug]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ltd|first=GardensOnline Pty|title=Aeonium haworthii {{!}} GardensOnline|url=https://www.gardensonline.com.au/gardenshed/plantfinder/show_3694.aspx|access-date=2021-04-07|website=www.gardensonline.com.au}}</ref> It is a sand-dwelling beach plant, a subshrub with rough, woody stems and rosettes of thick, red-edged green leaves which are triangular or diamond- or spade-shaped.<ref name=":1" />

==Description==
[[File:Aeonium haworthii PICT3759.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Inflorescence]]
It grows as a densely branched small shrub and reaches stature heights of up to {{Convert|60|cm|sp=us}}. The almost bare, somewhat mesh-like, ascending or hanging, winding shoots have a diameter of 3 to 6 millimeters. Their rather flat [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]]s reach a diameter of 6 to 11 centimeters. The inner leaves are more or less upright. The [[obovate]], green or yellowish green, often very heavily bluish, almost bare leaves are 3 to 5.5 centimeters long, 1.5 to 3 centimeters wide and 0.25 to 0.4 centimeters thick. They are pointed and trimmed towards the top. The base is wedge-shaped. The [[leaf margin]] is covered with curved eyelashes that are 0.4 to 0.8 millimeters long. The leaves are often reddish variegated along the edge.<ref>Reto Nyffeler: Aeonium haworthii . In: Urs Eggli (ed.): Succulent plant dictionary. Crassulaceae (thick leaf family) . Eugen Ulmer, Stuttgart 2003, {{ISBN|3-8001-3998-7}} , p. 17 .</ref>

It has [[panicle]]s of cream-colored pointed [[flower]]s produced in spring.<ref name=":2" /> The loose, hemispherical [[inflorescence]] has a length of {{Convert|6 to 16|cm|sp=us}} and a width of 6 to 16 centimeters {{Convert|60|cm|sp=us}}. The [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]] is 1 to 9 centimeters long. The seven-to nine-digit flowers are on a 2 to 12 millimeter long, bare flower stem. Its [[sepal]]s are bald. The pale yellow to whitish, pink [[variegated]], lanceolate, pointed petals are 7 to 9 millimeters long and 1.2 to 1.8 millimeters wide. The [[stamen]]s are almost glabrous to sparsely weak downy.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=1405332964|pages=1136}}</ref>
